title: Drill collar
description:
The surface location and orientation of a drillhole — the anchor every downhole record references.

GENERATED from the normative OpenAPI document (`spec/openapi.yaml`) — do not edit by hand; run `python scripts/regenerate.py`. The OpenAPI document is normative for the wire; this file is the same contract for one record type, readable on its own.
x-generated-by: scripts/regenerate.py from spec/openapi.yaml (geoDB Open Exploration Protocol v0.1.0)

hole_type.description: How the hole was drilled — the project's own drilling-method code (diamond core, reverse circulation, auger, and so on). Read the enum on this field for the values this server emits.

total_depth.description: The final drilled depth of the hole, in `length_units`. The depth measured ALONG the hole, not a vertical depth.

azimuth.description: Azimuth in DEGREES, clockwise from grid north (0–360). On a collar it is the orientation the hole was set up to drill; on a downhole survey station it is the measured orientation at that depth.

dip.description: Dip in DEGREES from horizontal. ⚠️ NEGATIVE IS DOWNWARD: a vertical hole drilled straight down is -90, a horizontal hole is 0. On a collar it is the set-up inclination; on a survey station it is the measured inclination at that depth.

display_units.description: Units the *_display strings on this record are formatted in, from the project's display preference. Presentation only: the stored values remain in `length_units`.

latitude.description:
⚠️ NOT necessarily degrees. This is the ORIGINAL as-imported coordinate in the CRS named by `epsg`: for a projected CRS (UTM, State Plane, ...) `longitude` holds the EASTING and `latitude` holds the NORTHING. The values are true WGS84 degrees only when `epsg` is 4326.

The field names are historical and are kept for continuity. For an unambiguous form of the same values, read `source_coordinate`; for WGS84, read `geometry` (EWKT) or `geometry_geojson`.

longitude.description:
⚠️ NOT necessarily degrees. This is the ORIGINAL as-imported coordinate in the CRS named by `epsg`: for a projected CRS (UTM, State Plane, ...) `longitude` holds the EASTING and `latitude` holds the NORTHING. The values are true WGS84 degrees only when `epsg` is 4326.

The field names are historical and are kept for continuity. For an unambiguous form of the same values, read `source_coordinate`; for WGS84, read `geometry` (EWKT) or `geometry_geojson`.

epsg.description: EPSG code of the coordinate reference system that `latitude`, `longitude` and `source_coordinate` are expressed in — the CRS the data was imported in, preserved rather than normalised. Interpret those values against this code; they are degrees only when it is 4326. The derived WGS84 form is always in `geometry` / `geometry_geojson`.

elevation.description: Elevation of the collar, in `elevation_units`. See `elevation_source` for whether it was surveyed, taken from a DEM, or entered by hand.

elevation_source.description:
Source of elevation data for quality tracking

* `surveyed` - Surveyed
* `dem` - DEM
* `manual` - Manual Entry
* `unknown` - Unknown

length_units.description: Units the record's DEPTH and LENGTH values are stored in: `M` (metres) or `FT` (feet). Stored units, not a display preference — read every depth against this.

xy_units.description: Get XY units for original coordinates (degrees, meters, feet, us-feet).

crs_xy_units.description: Get project CRS XY units (degrees, meters, feet, us-feet).

crs_elevation_units.description: Get project CRS elevation units (M or FT).

proj4_easting.description: Get local grid easting (X coordinate in custom Proj4 CRS).

proj4_northing.description: Get local grid northing (Y coordinate in custom Proj4 CRS).

proj4_elevation.description: Get local grid elevation (Z coordinate in custom Proj4 CRS).

proj4_xy_units.description: Get Proj4 local grid XY units (usually 'meters').

proj4_elevation_units.description: Get Proj4 local grid elevation units (M or FT).

geometry.description:
The derived WGS84 location as an EWKT string: `SRID=4326;POINT Z (lon lat elev)` — longitude first, then latitude, then elevation in metres (`POINT` without `Z` when no elevation is recorded). Always EPSG 4326, whatever `epsg` says.

This is the reprojected value. The original coordinate the customer supplied is `source_coordinate`. For a parsed object rather than a string, read `geometry_geojson`.

documents.description: Attached records, each as an object carrying its id, its natural key and display metadata. Soft-deleted attachments are omitted.

images.description: Attached records, each as an object carrying its id, its natural key and display metadata. Soft-deleted attachments are omitted.

source_coordinate.description: `{x, y, epsg}` — the original coordinate, unambiguously named (R2).

x.description: Easting, or longitude in degrees when epsg is 4326.

y.description: Northing, or latitude in degrees when epsg is 4326.

epsg.description: EPSG code x and y are expressed in.

coordinate_system_metadata.description: The project's coordinate-system settings (declared EPSG, optional local-grid proj4 string, units). Present on every record whose model carries a location. Advisory metadata for clients that reproject; the per-record CRS is always the record's own `epsg`.

^cf_[a-z0-9_]+$.description: Custom field. Any number of `cf_*` keys may be present: they are the project's user-defined fields, flattened to top level. The set of keys and their types vary BY PROJECT and BY MODEL — discover them at `/api/v2/model-schemas/?project_id=<id>`, never by assuming a fixed set. Values are whatever the customer stored (string, number, boolean or null). Calculated custom fields appear under the same prefix and are read-only.
